title: Skeletal pushouts of a simplicial tensor coend
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a category enriched over small simplicial sets [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set], with chosen tensors and cotensors as in [def-coef-simplicial-tensor-cotensor], and with all small colimits in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Write $A\otimes K$ for the tensor $K\otimes A$. Let $X:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal C$ be any simplicial object. For each $n\geq0$ define
$$R_n(X)=\operatorname{coeq}\left(\coprod_{\alpha:[a]\to[b],\;0\leq a,b\leq n}X_b\otimes\Delta^a\rightrightarrows\coprod_{a=0}^nX_a\otimes\Delta^a\right),$$
where $\Delta^a=\operatorname{Hom}_{\Delta}(-,[a])$, and the arrows on the $\alpha$ summand are induced by $X(\alpha)$ and $\Delta^\alpha$. Let $R_{-1}(X)$ be initial. Define $|X|$ by the same coequalizer without the upper bounds. Let $L_nX$ be the colimit over proper order-preserving surjections $\theta:[n]\twoheadrightarrow[a]$ with $a<n$, assigning $X_a$ to $\theta$; a morphism from $\theta$ to $\theta'$ is a surjection $\rho:[a']\twoheadrightarrow[a]$ with $\theta=\rho\theta'$, and its diagram map is $X(\rho):X_a\to X_{a'}$. The maps $X(\theta)$ induce $\lambda_n:L_nX\to X_n$. Let $\partial\Delta^n$ be the union of the proper faces of $\Delta^n$, with $\partial\Delta^0=\varnothing$. Set
$$B_n=(L_nX\otimes\Delta^n)\amalg_{L_nX\otimes\partial\Delta^n}(X_n\otimes\partial\Delta^n).$$
There is a pushout square with top edge $B_n\to R_{n-1}(X)$, left edge the canonical map $B_n\to X_n\otimes\Delta^n$, bottom edge the degree-$n$ coend map $X_n\otimes\Delta^n\to R_n(X)$, and right edge $R_{n-1}(X)\to R_n(X)$.
Here the upper arrow on the latching summand is induced, for each $\theta:[n]\twoheadrightarrow[a]$, by $X_a\otimes\Delta^n\xrightarrow{1\otimes\Delta^\theta}X_a\otimes\Delta^a\to R_{n-1}(X)$; on a boundary face $\delta:[a]\hookrightarrow[n]$ it is induced by $X_n\otimes\Delta^a\xrightarrow{X(\delta)\otimes1}X_a\otimes\Delta^a\to R_{n-1}(X)$. These maps agree on their overlaps. The truncation inclusions induce a natural isomorphism $\operatorname{colim}_{n\geq0}R_n(X)\cong|X|$. The square and isomorphism are natural in $X$. No model structure or cofibrancy assumption is required.
